label: input token j
explanation: A token detector for the input letter j. It fires on every step whose input is j: original-phase j and j fed back during the copy phase, at any position and for any L. It essentially never fires on any other input (about 84 dev steps on input 1) and never on <DEL>. Magnitude: the largest activations, near max, are j as the last original token right before <DEL>. j at t=0 is also strong (about 0.93 of max). Copy-phase j, and j in the middle of the original phase, are weaker (about 0.5-0.7 of max) in the examples.

issues: Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.9996, F1 0.9998, mass recall 0.9999, correlation 0.984. There are no false positives: every input-j step fires.

The 72 missed test steps are almost all input '1' as the last original token just before <DEL> (one case is '1' fed back in the copy phase). They are weak (about 0.14-0.20 of max) and carry 0.0% of the activation mass. This is a small, consistent leak, but it is negligible and the explanation already mentions it ('about 84 dev steps on input 1').
Delimiter-phase activation is 0, which confirms it never fires on <DEL>. The original and copy phases both fire at rate 0.033, which confirms it fires in both phases at any position and any L.

The magnitude claims match the profile examples. The top activations are all j as the last original token before <DEL> (0.97-1.00 of max). j at t=0 is about 0.93. Mid-sequence and copy-phase j are about 0.5-0.7. These come from examples only, as the explanation itself says.
The label 'input token j' matches the predicate exactly and does not overclaim.
